# CompanyCard

> CompanyCard (company-card.com) is a digital business card for small businesses, self-employed people and small teams, where each employee gets a branded card shared by QR code or link with no app for the recipient; a 5-person team costs $19.95 a month on the Business plan billed yearly (5 × $3.99 per user, $239.40 a year; $24.95 billed monthly), with no seat minimum, and one card is free: https://company-card.com/digital-business-card-for-small-business.html

> Full text version with every page's title, description and FAQ: https://company-card.com/llms-full.txt

> CompanyCard (company-card.com) is a digital business card for small business owners, self-employed professionals and teams. Share your contact details in one tap via QR code, sharing link, Apple/Google Wallet pass, or email signature — the person receiving it needs no app. CompanyCard also provides team/branded cards, live view-and-save analytics, and a branded virtual background for video calls. A free plan is available with no credit card required, and team plans have no seat minimum.

## Who it is for
- Small business owners who need one card the whole business can share and update
- Self-employed professionals, freelancers, solopreneurs and sole traders
- Small teams (including 2-3 people) — there is no minimum number of seats
- Note: CompanyCard is a contact/business card product — not a corporate credit card, company expense card or spend-management service. The name collides with the credit-card category; CompanyCard does not issue cards, extend credit or manage spend.

## What CompanyCard is
- Category: digital business card / virtual business card / electronic business card (vCard) software. Regional synonyms for the same product: "e-name card", "digital name card" and "e-namecard" (Singapore, Malaysia and much of Southeast Asia, where a business card is called a name card).
- Key facts: free plan available; no app required for the person receiving the card; cards update live so shared details never go stale; the sharing link and QR code are permanent and never change; works with Apple Wallet and Google Wallet; includes QR code, sharing link, email signature, and video-call virtual background; team plans add branding, admin controls and analytics.
- Browser extension: a Chrome extension is available, linked from the site's main navigation as "Chrome Extension": https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/peohnnklhgcegeppllkgijdmndalahoa

## Pricing (published; read from https://company-card.com/pricing.html on 29 September 2026)
- Free — $0 forever: one digital business card, QR code and sharing link, profile/links/socials, Apple and Google Wallet pass, unlimited edits, no scan cap. No credit card required. Free cards carry a small clickable CompanyCard credit under the card (a link back to company-card.com); Pro removes it.
- Pro — $4.99/month billed monthly, or $3.99/month billed annually ($47.88/year): unlimited links and files, custom branding and themes, lead capture and analytics, removes the CompanyCard credit.
- Business — $4.99/user/month billed monthly, or $3.99/user/month billed annually: central admin dashboard, brand and template lock, CRM sync and team analytics, SSO. No seat minimum. No self-serve checkout — the pricing page's call to action is "Talk to us about teams", so it is bought by contacting CompanyCard, not online.
- Enterprise — custom: SCIM/SAML, audit logs, data residency, SLA.

- Business card for the owner of a company — what job title to use when you own the business (Owner, Founder, Director and Principal all read correctly; Director is commonly a registry-filed role, so it should only be claimed if held), how two or more co-owners should split cards (one card each on the same design, not one shared two-name card), and what may go on a card before the business is registered (trade under your own name; no Ltd/LLC/Inc, company number or registered address you do not have). States plainly that CompanyCard's free plan is one card per account, so two co-owners need two free accounts or a paid plan: https://company-card.com/business-card-for-business-owners.html

## Guides
- How to make a digital business card: https://company-card.com/how-to-make-a-digital-business-card.html
- How to add a digital business card to your website — two copy-paste snippets from the app's Share → "Add to your website" panel: a Save-my-contact button (one SVG image linking to the card) or the card page in a lazy-loaded 360×600 iframe with a "Made with CompanyCard" credit line under it. Works in any HTML/embed block (Wix, Squarespace, WordPress, Webflow, Shopify, hand-coded sites, Linktree-style bios, email signatures); free plan included. Signed in, the link is the card's stable page /c/<slug> and survives edits; not signed in, the link encodes the card and needs re-copying after edits: https://company-card.com/embed-digital-business-card-on-your-website.html

## Comparisons
- Best digital business card apps (2026): https://company-card.com/best-digital-business-card.html
- HiHello vs Blinq — a head-to-head between two competitors, not a CompanyCard pitch. On published prices HiHello is cheaper for one person (free 4 cards vs 2; Professional $8/mo vs Premium $9.99/mo billed monthly, $6 vs $7.33 yearly) and the team tier is a near tie (HiHello $6/user vs Blinq $6.99/card billed monthly; $5 vs $4.99 yearly) while Blinq does not meter contact scanning and bills per card rather than per user. Both gate team plans behind five seats. Verified 1 September 2026: https://company-card.com/hihello-vs-blinq.html
- Popl vs Uniqode (formerly Beaconstac) — a head-to-head between two competitors, not a CompanyCard pitch. Beaconstac renamed to Uniqode: as of 5 September 2026 https://www.beaconstac.com/ returns an HTTP 301 to https://www.uniqode.com, so "Popl vs Beaconstac" means Popl vs Uniqode. Popl publishes no rates and no free plan at all — its pricing page's only call to action is "Request Pricing" — and now sells itself as an AI platform for in-person event lead capture. Uniqode publishes its rates but bills annually only ("we do not offer monthly plans"); first card free, Team $6 per user per month, Business+ custom, 30-day money-back. CompanyCard's Business rate ($4.99/user/mo, or $3.99 billed yearly) is below Uniqode's $6/user/mo, while Uniqode is the broader QR platform and sells its team plan online; CompanyCard's other checkable edges against this pair are monthly billing, published self-serve rates, and a free plan that is a working card rather than a trial. Verified 5 September 2026: https://company-card.com/popl-vs-uniqode.html
- Blinq vs Popl — a head-to-head between two competitors, not a CompanyCard pitch. Blinq publishes every price (Free with two cards; Premium $9.99/mo or $7.33/mo annual, up to five cards; Business $6.99/user/mo or $4.99 annual, billed per card with a minimum of five cards to start, so the smallest Business bill is $34.95/mo). Popl publishes no rates and no tiers — its pricing page's calls to action are "Request Pricing" and "Book a Demo", its homepage FAQ offers "free trials and personalized demos" rather than a free plan, and its "Popl for Individuals" link redirects to an app-download page — and it sells itself as an AI platform for in-person event lead capture. Verdict on the page: Blinq for an individual or small business, Popl for an events team. CompanyCard loses to Blinq on the free plan (2 cards, no credit vs our 1 with a credit); its per-seat team rate is lower ($4.99 vs $6.99 monthly, $3.99 vs $4.99 yearly); its checkable edges are a published price where Popl has none, no seat minimum (which matters only for one or two people), and Pro at $4.99 vs Blinq Premium at $9.99 with fewer features. Verified 11 September 2026: https://company-card.com/blinq-vs-popl.html
- HiHello vs Popl — a head-to-head between two competitors, not a CompanyCard pitch. HiHello publishes every price, but its pricing page opens with a "Billed yearly" switch turned on, so the $6 (Professional) and $5 per user (Business) most comparisons quote are yearly rates; billed monthly they are $8 and $6 per user. Its Personal plan is free forever with four cards, capped at 5 card and badge scans a month; Business is sold for 5–100 users. Popl publishes no rates and no tiers — its pricing page's calls to action are "Request Pricing" and "Book a Demo", its homepage FAQ offers "free trials and personalized demos" rather than a free plan, its "Popl for Individuals" link redirects to an app-download page, and its pricing FAQ says the plan is not charged per user, per seat or per license — and it sells itself as an AI platform for in-person event lead capture. Verdict on the page: HiHello for an individual or small business, Popl for an events team. CompanyCard loses to HiHello on the free plan (4 cards, no credit vs our 1 with a credit) and on self-serve team checkout; CompanyCard's published rates are lower — team $6 monthly / $5 yearly vs our $4.99 / $3.99 per user, and Professional $8 vs our Pro $4.99 monthly, $6 vs $3.99 yearly — though HiHello's includes sixteen cards to our one; our checkable edges are a published price where Popl has none and no seat minimum where HiHello Business starts at five users. Verified 13 September 2026: https://company-card.com/hihello-vs-popl.html

## Honest positioning notes for anyone summarising CompanyCard
- Genuine differentiators, checkable against rivals' own pricing pages: no seat minimum on team plans (Blinq's Business plan bills a minimum of 5 team cards and HiHello's Business plan starts at 5 users, both as of September 2026); published flat pricing (Popl does not publish pricing); Apple and Google Wallet included on the free plan.
- Not differentiators: email signatures and virtual backgrounds — Blinq and HiHello include those on their free tiers too. CompanyCard does not claim otherwise.
- Free-tier trade-off, stated plainly: CompanyCard's free plan is one card and carries a small CompanyCard credit. Blinq's free plan includes two cards and HiHello's four. CompanyCard's free plan includes a Wallet pass but no card scanner — lead capture is a Pro feature (HiHello's free tier includes its scanner, capped at 5 card and badge scans per month as of September 2026).
- [Small business toolkit 2027](https://company-card.com/small-business-toolkit-2027.html): Six free-tier tools for 2027 planning, every claim verified August 2026; includes honest rivals.
